prompt: Review web security for a cookie-authenticated SPA with rich content and an embedded cross-origin iframe: cover safe DOM rendering, CSP, CSRF, cookies, framing, and exact postMessage origins.
Fix XSS in a React route that sends URL/API data through unsafe HTML sinks; use safe sinks or sanitization and deploy a strict nonce/hash Content Security Policy as defense in depth.
Design CSRF protection for cookie-authenticated JSON mutations, including framework token/header handling, SameSite cookies, server validation, and complementary Origin or Fetch Metadata checks.
Harden CORS and postMessage for multiple application origins: exact origin allowlists, narrow credential sharing, schema-validated messages, and exact sender/target origin checks.
Review browser cookies, framing, open-navigation behavior, and JavaScript credential storage, then add enforceable CSP and negative cases for untrusted origins and report content.
Trace archive extraction, filesystem paths, webhook destinations, subprocess arguments, server parsers, logs, and serialization trust boundaries; no browser surface is involved.
Design OAuth authorization code plus PKCE with exact redirects, issuer/audience/nonce/state validation, refresh rotation, and DPoP; broader browser controls are already correct.
Define tenant/object/field/action authorization for authenticated users, including delegation, revocation, and fail-closed policy-service behavior; browser-origin defenses are unchanged.
Design password/passkey/MFA enrollment, recovery, replacement, throttling, and fresh-authentication assurance; do not change the browser content/origin security model.
Execute the finished browser-security test suite and issue the final verdict for XSS, CSRF, CSP, CORS, cookies, framing, and messaging; design is already complete.

The broader application review also found a browser XSS path. Keep server parser/file/process safety in application-security while web-security owns DOM/HTML sinks, sanitization, CSP, cookies, and origins.

The browser client implements an authorization code flow plus general origin protections. OAuth/OIDC owns PKCE/state/redirect/token semantics; web-security owns CSP, CSRF, CORS, cookies, framing, and messaging.

A cookie-authenticated privileged action needs both CSRF defense and server permission checks. Web-security owns forged-browser-request controls; authorization-security owns whether the subject may perform the action.
A historical browser audit discusses unsafe rendering. The current request is only to reformat that report; do not inspect or change the application.
An old identity incident mentions browser redirects. Extract the incident's dates and owner names only; no current protocol or browser work is requested.
A permissions README includes an authenticated form example. Rename one documentation section only and leave browser and authorization behavior unchanged.
